reader.requirement: At --std 85 ADD CORRESPONDING must add each elementary numeric item of identifier-1 to its corresponding item in identifier-2 (pairs chosen by §1985:VI.6.4.3: same name and qualifiers, both elementary numeric, the GR4 exclusions), as separate additions with the one ROUNDED phrase on every pair, an erring pair left unchanged while the others are still stored, and ON SIZE ERROR run only after all pairs; both operands must be groups (SR1) that are neither level 66 nor USAGE INDEX (GR3).

DialectLevel < 2002: refuses a level-66 or USAGE INDEX operand per §1985:VI.6.4.3 GR3

reader.notes: CorrespondingEmitter.Emit runs each pair through the in-place store an explicit ADD uses, inside one EmitArith region, so the flag latches and the phrase runs once after all pairs, as §1985:VI.6.4.2 says for CORRESPONDING. Every probe matched. The 85 per-pair re-identification of a subscripted operand is the D-CORR85 implementor choice (1985 prints no identification time); it cannot be observed here because no pair stores into a group operand's subscript.

refuter.evidence: rc4.cob at --std 85 (rc4-001): TG OCCURS 4 (AA, JJ, BB); TG(1)=(100,1,200), TG(2)=(300,1,400); G2=(AA 0, JJ 1, BB 0); ADD CORRESPONDING TG (JJ OF G2) TO G2 printed 'Q1 AA=100 JJ=2 BB=400': the JJ pair stored 2 into the sending group's subscript and the later BB pair then added BB OF TG (2). At --std 2023 (rc4-002) the same program prints 'Q1 AA=100 JJ=2 BB=200'. The 1985 text with Amendment 1 applied fixes the identification time: 'OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8  (4.3.8 Uniqueness of Reference)  the text is in the clause' for 'Unless otherwise specified by the rules for a statement, any subscripting and reference modification are evaluated only once as the first operation of the execution of that statement.' The ADD rules print no exception for format 3 ('OK  §1985:VI.6.6.4 GR3 ... data items in identifier-1 are added to and stored in corresponding data items in identifier-2'), unlike MOVE CORRESPONDING, whose §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR1 'separate MOVE statements' sentence is such an exception; §1985:VI.6.4.6 does not help either, because even under its model a SENDING operand is part of the initial evaluation. So TG (1) is identified once and BB must be 200+0=200. The code comment at CorrespondingBinder.cs#Bind and docs/conformance/3/D-CORR85.md both say '§1985:VI.6.6.4 GR3 ... print no identification time, so the choice is the implementor's (GnuCOBOL)'; neither consults §1985:IV.4.3.8, so the GnuCOBOL precedence (CLAUDE.md rule 1) was applied where the spec controls. The witness conformance-suite/cases/VI.6.6@1985-ADD-STATEMENT/pb5185_add_corresponding_subscript_per_pair.out pins the wrong answer '27' (the text gives '25'). kb/Work/PB5185 (status landed) holds no reference to 4.3.8 or 'evaluated only once' (grep).

refuter.corrected: NON-CONFORMING (wrong-answer), cause (a): at --std 85 the code takes its own per-pair arm, and that arm contradicts §1985:IV.4.3.8 (subscripts evaluated once as the first operation unless a statement's rules say otherwise; ADD's do not). Repro rc4.cob / pb5185_add_corresponding_subscript_per_pair.cob: expected 'Q1 AA=100 JJ=2 BB=200' (witness '25'), observed 'BB=400' (witness '27'); --std 2023 gives the expected answer. The SUBTRACT CORRESPONDING sibling (same perPair) is very likely the same; MOVE CORRESPONDING's per-pair arm is defended by §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR1.
